idea: Every F, PRF, H and T_l of the SHA-2 sets is one SHA-256 compression (or a few) from a chaining value that is fixed for the key. The ESP32-C3 SHA accelerator can start from a loaded chaining value, keeps it in the byte order of the standard, and keeps its message registers between compressions; slhdsa-c's instantiation interface (function pointers per hash) lets a second instantiation replace only the hashes.
change: suites/slhdsa/pqc_suite/slh_sha2_c3.c: F, PRF, chain, H and T_l on the accelerator registers; midstate written straight to the H registers, only changed message words written (5 of 16 inside a chain for n = 16), address and padding words tracked in a copy in RAM, only n bytes read back. slh_glue.c: backend switch in front of slhdsa-c's primitives.
note: Key generation 130137 -> 8045 us, verification 176721 -> 11954 us. About 280 cycles per hash against 4200 for slhdsa-c's SHA-256 in C. Still the code used for single hashes; slhdsa-02 builds on it. 'after' is from the build of that moment.

idea: The accelerator needs about 80 cycles per compression and copies the block when it starts. While it works on one hash the block of another can be written, so the wait is not idle. The next block of a chain is unknown until its previous step is read back, so advance two independent chains in turn.
change: slh_sha2_c3_tmpl.h: wots_pkgen (all chains of a WOTS+ key, two at a time, then T_l), fors_leaf2 (two FORS leaves at a time), wots_chains (the chains of a WOTS+ signature, two slots). third_party/slhdsa-c: three optional members in slh_param_s and three guarded call sites in slh_dsa.c, because per-hash function pointers cannot express this.
note: Key generation 8045 -> 5641 us, verification 11954 -> 10619 us. About 195 cycles per hash in a WOTS+ key. suites/slhdsa/hosttest runs the same code against a register-level model of the accelerator on the build machine, so the logic was tested before each board run.

idea: The two-slot scheduler of the verification chains indexed its slots with a variable, which kept both chain values in memory. Give each slot its own copy of the code so that both stay in registers.
change: slh_sha2_c3_tmpl.h: wots_chains rewritten with a STEP macro instantiated for slot a and slot b

idea: For n = 24 and 32 the standard uses SHA-512 for H and T_l, which the accelerator does not have; after slhdsa-02 it is about two thirds of signing. Use a SHA-512 written in C for 32-bit halves instead of slhdsa-c's.
change: slh_glue.c: sha2_512_compress() routed to components/prims/opt/sha512_rv32.c (both removed again)
note: No separate 'before': per block the C rewrite was 85.0 us in slhdsa-c's layout against 84.8 for slhdsa-c's own code (suites/hashes), so 1193577 us is in effect the time with slhdsa-c's SHA-512. No gain; see hashes-06.

idea: PQClean's SHA-512 in components/prims is 4 % faster per block than slhdsa-c's; use it for the optimized variant.
note: Never ran: PQClean's compression function is 42 KB of straight-line code and the image overflowed the RAM segment by 16.6 KB.

idea: SHA-512 in assembly with all working variables in registers (hashes-07), and H and T_l for n = 24 and 32 written on top of it from a midstate stored as native words, so the chaining value is not byte-swapped on every call.
change: slh_sha2_c3.c: h512, tl512, native SHA-512 midstate; components/prims/opt/sha512_rv32imc.S (block as bytes)
note: Key generation 17480 -> 15912 us, verification 67200 -> 57107 us (includes slhdsa-03). SLH-DSA-SHA2-256f signing 2701641 -> 2344682 us. Replaced by slhdsa-07 and -08.

idea: Three quarters of a 256s signature is H on FORS tree nodes, and each call spent about 1100 cycles around the compression: copying the address byte by byte, two unaligned copies, clearing the padding, byte-wise loading inside the assembly. Build the block of H from words, keep padding and length in place between calls, and hand the assembly native words (hashes-08).
change: slh_sha2_c3.c: h512 builds the block from words into a persistent buffer; tl512 converts its blocks; sha512_rv32imc.S takes native words
note: Signing 2 % faster on all four sets (192f: 1033180 -> 1021436 us), but key generation and verification 1 to 3 % slower (192f keygen 15912 -> 16383 us): T_l now copied and byte-swapped every block in C. Fixed by slhdsa-08.

idea: Most blocks of T_l lie entirely inside the input. Convert those straight from the input bytes into the word buffer instead of copying them to a block buffer first.
change: slh_sha2_c3.c: tl512 fast path for whole blocks

idea: No hardware for Keccak. Use the project's optimized Keccak-f[1600], and write F, PRF, H and the chain step directly on the 25 lanes instead of going through slhdsa-c's incremental SHA-3 interface (clear, absorb byte by byte, pad, squeeze byte by byte): each of these hashes is exactly one permutation and its inputs start on lane boundaries.
change: suites/slhdsa/pqc_suite/slh_shake_fast.c; slh_glue.c routes keccak_f1600() to pqc_keccakf1600()
checked: acvp-kat+fingerprint+host build of the same file
note: 1.50x, the same factor on all six SHAKE sets and all three operations. Almost all of it is the permutation (118 -> 79 us, not this line of work); the two contributions were not measured separately on the board. 80 us per hash for a 79 us permutation, so little is left around it.

target: image memory (bytes free in the main RAM segment)
idea: The image with all 12 sets, both variants and four fully stored ACVP sigVer vectors left 10 KB of the main RAM segment free and crashed during start-up, before any output. Builds that left 20 KB ran.
change: suites/slhdsa/gen_kat.py: two of the four stored sigVer vectors dropped (one valid vector for SHA2-128s and one invalid for SHAKE-128s remain)
checked: board run of the final image, all checks pass
note: Not an optimization: a fix for a start-up crash (instruction access fault with a garbage address, seen twice with two different code sets). Why the start-up needs that much of this segment was not investigated.
